newsitem.title: MONACO: SOCCER SHOWCASE-BARTHEZ LOOKS FORWARD TO MEETING FORMER CLUB.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER SHOWCASE-BARTHEZ LOOKS FORWARD TO MEETING FORMER CLUB.

text.p: Meeting Marseille is definitely something special for Monaco goalkeeper Fabien Barthez, who burst into the limelight there before joining the principality.
Barthez, who helped Marseille win the European Cup by beating AC Milan in the Munich final in 1993, could reach another peak this season as Monaco are running away with the league title.
Saturday's match against his former club comes at a crucial moment from the balding, 25-year old Barthez, as he is currently pushing Bernard Lama for France's number one shirt.
Barthez is likely to replace Lama as the national team goalkeeper as the Paris St Germain international faces a possible two-month ban for testing positive for cannabis.
"Bernard's ban? It is just ridiculous," said Barthez, who was himself banned for two months in October 1995 after traces of cannabis were found in his urine.
"When people say that cannabis is used as a pain killer, it makes me laugh. I don't know whether it will allow me to become France's number one goalkeeper and I don't want to know," he added.
"But I also want to tell Bernard such an experience can be useful. It helped me work harder and prove than it was not thanks to cannabis that I was a good goalkeeper."
Barthez, who won his sixth cap against Sweden earlier this month, has established himself as one of Europe's finest goalkeepers thanks to superb reflexes and decisiveness coming out of goal.
After a short spell with Toulouse he made his breakthrough with Marseille, who were then at the top of European soccer under the rule of Bernard Tapie.

"This season, Monaco also play great matches in the league as well as on the European scene and that reminds me of my Marseille," he said shortly before Internazionale knocked out Monaco in a UEFA Cup semifinal clash on Tuesday.

"But the surroundings and the atmosphere are very different," he said, perhaps missing the passion that always accompanied Marseille. "Here, it's sometimes hard to believe that we are the league leaders."
Asked if he has improved over the past few years, Barthez said: "I played great matches in Marseille too but it's true that I'm playing much better now than when I joined Monaco (in 1995)."
Barthez, a popular character, is no ordinary player. He is so involved in the action on the field that he sometimes forgets he is a goalkeeper.
In the dying minutes of Tuesday's match against Internazionale he left his goal and joined the attack, as he often does.
"I can't stand losing and sometimes, I wish I could be the 11 players at the same time," he said. "We might still lose now and again but I would be the only one to blame for it."
